---
title: "One day – the housing-audit case"
subtitle: "Four parts of ninety minutes, with a facilitator"
---
The [case study](../../cases/housing/index.qmd), which presents the original study, the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and the SCORE replication on which both tracks of the case are built, is the place to start.

This is the one-day course on the housing-audit case. It brings the three strands of the course together, the computational tools, the statistics and the practices of open research, on one field experiment in which emails that differed only in the name that signed them were sent to public housing authorities in the United States. Across the day you work as analyst no. 6 on a claim of the original authors (OAs) that five analysts reanalysed for Multi100. You reproduce the value that Multi100 recorded for one of them, write the estimand statement behind the claim, finish a causal graph of the experiment, work through a menu of defensible analyses, and then declare one of them in a shortened preregistration template before you run it. What you leave with is a report of your own, two marks on the class chart, one explored and one declared, and the place of your result among the 64 specifications on the curve of the claim.

The day runs as four parts of ninety minutes, with breaks of thirty, sixty and thirty minutes between them. Several of its steps are things that the class does together, such as everyone typing the chi-square value they have just reproduced and holding it back until the facilitator says go, so the day needs a facilitator. Some stretches of the slides are optional, a short tour of the toolchain and of R in the morning and a closer look at the statistics in the afternoon, and the facilitator switches them on or off to suit the class. The [short session](../housing-short/index.qmd) covers the same case in two to three hours.

| | What happens | Length |
|---|---|---|
| [Before the day](before.qmd) | Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the workspace, read the case study. | 1 to 2 hours, once |
| [Part 1 – Credibility and tools](part-1.qmd) | What a claim is for, why the field talks of a crisis, the evidence on reproduction, robustness and replication, and the toolchain; then you get running. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 2 – The claim and its estimand](part-2.qmd) | The paper and the five analysts, estimands and the causal-graph crash course; you write the estimand statement and finish the graph. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 3 – Reproduction and exploration](part-3.qmd) | You reproduce the recorded result, then work the specification menu and put an exploratory mark on the class chart. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 4 – Multiverse, replication and preregistration](part-4.qmd) | The class reads its chart against the curve of 64, meets the replication with new data, and each participant declares one analysis, runs it and reports it. | 90 minutes |
| [After the day](after.qmd) | Where to go next in the companion curriculum. | as you like |
